scenarios.title: Adopt a database that already has a schema
scenarios.tagline: Record the history a database already earned, and let the operator carry on from there.
scenarios.learn: How baseline proves a database matches its migrations before recording anything, and what it refuses.
scenarios.start: A database an application created before Ptah: a shipments table with three rows, the state migration 1 produces, and no record that it ran. The lab inserted them as setup. Beside it, an empty PostgreSQL the lab stood up as the shadow baseline replays into, with its URL in the Secret demo-shadow-database.
events: # This database already has a shipments table and three rows. An application put them there.
kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE" exec deploy/demo-psql -- psql -c "SELECT * FROM shipments ORDER BY id"
# It has no Ptah history. There is no revision table at all.
# The sequence the operator will run holds two migrations, in these files.
# Hand the files to the cluster. Baseline reads them, and so will the resource.
# Baseline runs in the cluster. The target, a disposable shadow, and the version to record up to.
# Ptah's own baseline, as a Job, for a database the cluster can reach and a
# It replays the migration files into an empty shadow database and compares
# the schema they produce with the target's, through the version below. Only
# when the two agree does it write the history; otherwise it writes nothing.
# The image is a name to replace: kubectl set image puts in the executor image
# the chart runs, its executorImage value.
# The database to adopt, and a shadow that holds nothing else:
# baseline empties it before it replays anything.
# One mount per file: a ConfigMap volume is a directory of symlinks,
# and a reader that walks into it finds every file twice.
# Refused. Replayed into the shadow, the files make a carrier column this database lacks.

kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE" exec deploy/demo-psql -- psql -c "SELECT * FROM shipments ORDER BY id"

scenarios.title: Start a new database from a checkpoint
scenarios.tagline: A fresh database runs the snapshot and what came after it, and ends up where the long way ends.
scenarios.learn: What a checkpoint replaces, who selects it, and how the operator proves the shortcut arrived at the same place.
scenarios.start: An empty database with no migration history, and a namespace with the lab's Secrets, as Stand up the lab leaves them.
events: # Four versions, each with its down file, and one is not a migration. The name is the contract.
# The checkpoint records where migration 2 left the column, not where migration 1 created it.
-- What migrations 1 and 2 produce between them, as one file.
-- The name is the contract: `.checkpoint.` is what makes Ptah treat this as the
-- floor a fresh database starts from rather than a third migration. A database
-- that has already run 1 and 2 ignores it; a database that has run nothing runs
-- this and then 4, and ends up indistinguishable from one that replayed
-- The column is NOT NULL here because that is where migration 2 left it. A
-- checkpoint that recorded the column as it was created, before the backfill
-- and the constraint, would start a new database in a state the old one had
# Publish it, and point a resource at the whole artifact. Nothing in it names the checkpoint.
# Against a database with no history, under apply Always, it runs without waiting for anyone.
ptahmigration/shipments in namespace demo reached in-sync.
kubectl ptah migration shipments -n demo shows where it stands.
# An empty history let the checkpoint stand in for 1 and 2, and 4 ran after it. Nothing is left.
Ready:                True, HistoryMatched: The database has every migration this artifact carries
Progressing       False   HistoryMatched   <time>                Nothing is pending
ArtifactVerified  True    PolicySatisfied  <time>                The resolved artifact satisfied its verification policy
Blocked           False   HistoryMatched   <time>                The history continues this artifact
Ready             True    HistoryMatched   <time>                The database has every migration this artifact carries
ApprovalRequired  False   Satisfied        <time>                The plan's approval requirements are satisfied
kubectl events -n demo --for ptahmigration/shipments prints its Events.
# The table is what replaying all four would have built, down to the constraint.

scenarios.title: Manage reference data
scenarios.tagline: Rows declared beside the tables that hold them, reconciled through the same plan.
scenarios.learn: What a declared row set owns, how a change to rows alone reaches the database, and why removing a declaration is not a delete.
scenarios.start: An empty database and a namespace with the lab's Secrets, as Stand up the lab leaves them. The rows are declared in Go source, which ptah schema push publishes from its directory.
events: # A declaration names the table, the column that identifies a row, and the file the rows live in.
// Package catalog is the storefront's reference data: the tables whose rows the
// application reads and never writes, declared beside the tables themselves.
// The module compiles it and nothing imports it: what reads it is Ptah, which
// parses the annotations out of the source. It lives under demo/ rather than
// testdata/ because a reader publishes it by typing the path, and the path is
// part of what the demonstration shows.
// Two tables joined by a foreign key, because a reference set is usually
// several tables that have to arrive in an order the constraint allows.
// The country rows arrive in the next revision rather than here. Ptah emits
// declared rows grouped by table, in an order that ignores the dependency
// order it uses for the tables themselves, so a child row can be offered
// before the parent row it references and the foreign key refuses it
// (stokaro/ptah#3252). Declaring the parent first, and the child once the
// parent rows exist, is the sequence that works today.
# The rows themselves are a list, each one a map from column name to value.
name: Europe, Middle East and Africa
# Publish the directory, and create a resource that names it by digest.
# The tables are created and the declared rows are put in them.
ptahschema/catalog in namespace demo reached in-sync.
kubectl ptah schema catalog -n demo shows where it stands.
# The declared rows are in the table.
kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE" exec deploy/demo-psql -- psql -c "SELECT code, name FROM regions ORDER BY code"
emea | Europe, Middle East and Africa
# The child table exists and holds nothing. Its rows come in the next revision.
kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE" exec deploy/demo-psql -- psql -c "SELECT count(*) FROM countries"
# The second revision adds rows and no column. One marker, nothing else.
// parent rows exist, is the sequence that works today.
# Publish it, and point the resource at it. The rows are planned and applied.
Source set for ptahschema/catalog in namespace demo.

scenarios.title: Suspend and resume
scenarios.tagline: One field stops reconciliation without deleting anything, and resuming picks up where it stopped.
scenarios.learn: How to take a database out of the operator's hands during an incident, and give it back.
scenarios.start: Where Apply a schema ends: storefront converged on schemas/v1.sql, published as an artifact, under apply Always.
events: Ready:                True, InSync: Schema is in sync
Policy:               apply Always, allowDestructive false, driftSeverity all
EngineSupported       True    SupportedEngine  <time>                Database engine "PostgreSQL" is supported
Ready                 True    InSync           <time>                Schema is in sync
ReconciliationFailed  False   Succeeded        <time>                The latest operation completed
ArtifactResolved      True    DigestPinned     <time>                Desired OCI reference resolved to immutable content
ArtifactVerified      True    PolicySatisfied  <time>                Artifact type and verification policy were satisfied
DatabaseReachable     True    Observed         <time>                Database schema was observed
DriftDetected         False   ScopedConverged  <time>                The authoritative managed scope has no changes
InSync                True    ScopedConverged  <time>                A stable scoped plan proves convergence
ApprovalRequired      False   Satisfied        <time>                Current plan approval requirements are satisfied
PlanReady             False   NoChanges        <time>                No executable plan is required
Applying              False   JobCompleted     <time>                Apply Job completed; convergence observation is pending
Suspended             False   Active           <time>                Reconciliation is active
kubectl events -n demo --for ptahschema/storefront prints its Events.
# Suspend it. One field, and the resource stays exactly where it is.
Suspend requested for ptahschema/storefront in namespace demo.
The operator starts no new Job once it observes generation 2. Suspension cancels no SQL.
ptahschema/storefront in namespace demo reached suspended.
kubectl ptah schema storefront -n demo shows where it stands.
# Now publish a change it would otherwise pick up, and point the resource at it.
Source set for ptahschema/storefront in namespace demo.
Kept:      verificationPolicyFrom demo-verification-policy key policy.yaml, registryAuthFrom demo-registry, transport.plainHTTP true

Once the operator observes generation 3 it resolves the new reference, checks it against the verification policy, reads the database and plans from what it finds. A plan or an approval from the previous artifact does not carry over.
Under spec.policy.apply Always the operator applies that plan without a person, unless it is destructive or changes privileges: those wait for an approval.

set-source --wait waits in the same command until a plan from the new reference waits for an approval or the resource rests in sync from it; kubectl ptah wait, run later, counts only a reading that begins after it does.
# Nothing happens, which is the point. A wait gives up and names what holds it.
Waiting up to 30s for ptahschema/storefront in namespace demo to reach in-sync.
kubectl-ptah: ptahschema/storefront in namespace demo did not reach in-sync within 30s.
Held by:     Suspended=True, Requested: New database operations are suspended
Waiting for: a read of the database that began after the wait did (the last one is from <time>)
kubectl ptah schema storefront -n demo shows every condition with its message.
# Resume, and it starts from what is actually there rather than from what it remembered.
Resume requested for ptahschema/storefront in namespace demo.
Once the operator observes generation 4 it reads the database again and decides from what it finds.
ptahschema/storefront in namespace demo reached in-sync.
kubectl ptah schema storefront -n demo shows where it stands.
# It planned against the live database and converged on the revision it was given.

checks.claim: exits 0, prints "Suspend requested", prints "spec.suspend true", prints "reached suspended"
exits 7, reports "did not reach in-sync", reports "Suspended"

scenarios.title: Run a prepared migration sequence
scenarios.tagline: Numbered SQL files in an artifact, matched against the database's own record of what has run.
scenarios.learn: How the versioned workflow differs from the declarative one, and what the database is asked before anything executes.
scenarios.start: An empty database and a namespace with the lab's Secrets, as Stand up the lab leaves them, with no migration history.
events: # The sequence is files. Numbered, with a direction, and written by a person.
# The second one adds a column, fills it, and only then constrains it. Order is the point.
ALTER TABLE shipments ADD COLUMN carrier TEXT;
SET carrier = CASE WHEN reference LIKE 'EU-%' THEN 'dhl' ELSE 'ups' END;
ALTER TABLE shipments ALTER COLUMN carrier SET NOT NULL;
# Publish the directory, and create the resource that names it and asks for a person.
# The operator resolves the artifact, verifies it, and reads the database's history.
ptahmigration/shipments in namespace demo reached approval.
kubectl ptah approve migration/shipments -n demo reviews it.
# Two migrations pending against an empty history, and a plan waiting for a decision.
Ready:                False, AwaitingApproval: The plan is waiting for the approval its policy requires
ApprovalRequired: True, AwaitingApproval: 2 planned migrations need an approval naming this plan
Progressing       False   AwaitingApproval  <time>                Nothing runs until a person writes the approval
ArtifactVerified  True    PolicySatisfied   <time>                The resolved artifact satisfied its verification policy
Blocked           False   HistoryMatched    <time>                The history continues this artifact
Ready             False   AwaitingApproval  <time>                The plan is waiting for the approval its policy requires
ApprovalRequired  True    AwaitingApproval  <time>                2 planned migrations need an approval naming this plan
kubectl events -n demo --for ptahmigration/shipments prints its Events.
# No migration has run, and reading the history wrote nothing. The database is still empty.
# Approve it. The plan is versions and checksums, and the approval names its fingerprint.
A migration plan records versions and checksums. Its SQL is read from the
source the plan binds, and it is not shown here:
Approve plan ptah-mplan-e44496c57c4ba9bc4a85f1f4 of migration/shipments in demo? Type yes to approve: yes
Approved: PtahMigrationApproval demo/shipments-v1, recorded by admission as kubernetes-admin at <time>.
Waiting up to 5m0s for ptahmigration/shipments in namespace demo to reach applied.
ptahmigration/shipments in namespace demo reached applied.
kubectl ptah migration shipments -n demo shows where it stands.
# The sequence ran, and the column is constrained the way migration 2 left it.
# The verdict is the database's, read from the revision table and not from the Job's exit code.
Ready:                True, HistoryMatched: The database has every migration this artifact carries
plan ptah-mplan-e44496c57c4ba9bc4a85f1f4, not the current plan
Consumed  True    DispatchCommitted  <time>                The approved plan was dispatched
Progressing       False   HistoryMatched   <time>                Nothing is pending
ArtifactVerified  True    PolicySatisfied  <time>                The resolved artifact satisfied its verification policy
Blocked           False   HistoryMatched   <time>                The history continues this artifact
Ready             True    HistoryMatched   <time>                The database has every migration this artifact carries
ApprovalRequired  False   Satisfied        <time>                The plan's approval requirements are satisfied
kubectl events -n demo --for ptahmigration/shipments prints its Events.
# Read the history again. There is nothing pending, so nothing runs.
Read requested for ptahmigration/shipments in namespace demo.
Observed: phase InSync, last read at <time>

The request is written, not answered. The operator takes it once no operation is running, the resource is not suspended and no retry delay is pending, and a read already under way does not answer it. It starts no Apply and approves nothing.
ptahmigration/shipments in namespace demo reached read.
kubectl ptah migration shipments -n demo shows where it stands.
